battu.tu-binh-con-goi-bat-tu.t: Zi Ping (also called BaZi) is a method of reading destiny from the four pillars — the stems and branches of your birth year, month, day and hour — and took shape in the Song dynasty. With the Day Master as the reference point, it compares the other pillars to find the useful god and the chart structure, and reads a whole life from there.

battu.tu-tru-khong-doan-may-rui.t: The Four Pillars don't guess at luck. They point straight at which of the five elements your chart lacks — the reason some stretches of life go smoothly while others feel like swimming upstream. Cast your chart to see what you're missing.

luangiai.tu-vi-dau-so-la-mot.t: Zi Wei Dou Shu (Purple Star Astrology) is a traditional system of Chinese destiny reading. It casts a chart from the lunar birth hour, with 12 palaces and a system of major and minor stars. Refined over many generations, it became popular in Vietnam through the translation of Zi Wei Dou Shu Xin Bian (Tử Vi Đẩu Số Tân Biên) by Vân Đằng Thái Thứ Lang, and grew into a distinct Vietnamese school.

luangiai.tu-vi-khong-du-doan-tuong.t: Zi Wei doesn't predict the future. It helps you understand yourself so you can choose better.

napam.moi-nam-sinh-mang-mot-menh.t: Every birth year carries its own Na Yin element — which decides the colors and directions that suit you, though few people notice. Enter your birth year and get the full element name, its element, and your matching colors and directions, free.

napam.nap-am-la-phep-phoi-hanh.t: Na Yin (Sound of the Five Elements) assigns a Five Element to each stem-branch pair in the Sexagenary cycle (60 years), giving every birth year an element with its own name, such as Metal in the Sea or Earth by the Roadside. It is one branch of the applied Five Elements system in classical Chinese numerology.
